title: Telangana State Consumer Commission (order 10 Nov 2026): a UPI PIN alone doesn't prove a customer authorised a payment; SBI to pay ₹85,000 (₹55,000 refund + ₹20,000 compensation + ₹10,000 costs); with RBI's current 3-working-day zero-liability rule and its new 5-calendar-day rules from 1 Jan 2027
format: news carousel (consumer ruling + what RBI's rules give fraud victims now and from 1 Jan 2027), cover + 3 detail slides
headline: Consumer Panel: UPI PIN Alone Isn't Proof, SBI Owes ₹85,000

fact_sources.fact: Telangana State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (President Mamidi Christopher; members S Sandhya Rani, K Venkateshwarlu) passed the order on 10 Nov 2026
₹55,000 debited from a 44-year-old woman's SBI account by UPI on 3 Nov 2022; she says she never made or authorised it
SBI argued UPI PIN + mobile/SIM-binding authentication meant she authorised it or exposed credentials, and that she reported late
Commission: use of a UPI PIN does not by itself/automatically establish authorisation or negligence; bank must show it; no evidence she made the transaction or shared credentials
Complaint on cybercrime portal 6 Nov 2022, written complaint at branch 7 Nov 2022; Sunday excluded, so within three working days
SBI to pay ₹55,000 refund + ₹20,000 compensation + ₹10,000 costs = ₹85,000

RBI 2017 rule (RBI/2017-18/15, 6 Jul 2017): third-party breach notified within 3 working days = zero liability; bank's own fault = zero liability regardless; 4-7 working days = liability capped per transaction at ₹5,000/₹10,000/₹25,000 by account type; burden of proof on the bank
RBI directions RBI/2026-27/167 issued 24 Jun 2026 apply to electronic banking transactions on or after 1 Jan 2027
2027 rules: zero liability for third-party breach reported to the bank within 5 calendar days
2027 rules: customers asked to report to the bank and to NCRP (cybercrime.gov.in) or 1930
2027 rules: burden of proving customer liability lies on the bank

2027 rules: one-time (once in a lifetime) compensation of 85% of net loss or ₹25,000, whichever is less, for gross losses up to ₹50,000, including customer-negligence cases, if reported to the bank and NCRP/1930 within 5 calendar days; frauds up to one year after 1 Jan 2027

not_used: RBI 2027 text defines covered transactions as 'electronic funds transfer' under the PSS Act and doesn't name UPI, so the RBI 2027 slide doesn't say 'UPI'. SBI appeal status unknown, so the order isn't called final. The ₹10,000 savings-account cap is RBI-only, so the slide uses the ₹5,000-₹25,000 range (RBI + The Better India).
